prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1243; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received from the insured's driver reporting a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection, with the claimant's vehicle stopped in front. A claim file has been opened and the policy was confirmed active with the driver listed as a named driver.

Entry 2: Spoke with the claimant's representing attorney, who confirmed the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of the collision and is reporting neck pain consistent with whiplash. A letter of representation is on file and all further contact will go through counsel.

Entry 3: Reviewed the police report, which confirms the claimant's vehicle was stopped and was struck from behind, and the responding officer documented the claimant at the scene. No independent witnesses were identified in the report.

Entry 4: Photographs of both vehicles were received and reviewed. They confirm the general location of the damage, and the rear damage on the claimant's vehicle is mostly in line with the impact described by the insured's driver.

Entry 5: Took a recorded statement from the claimant through counsel. The account of how the collision happened matches what was described in the first notice, and the claimant has given the same account in every conversation so far.

Entry 6: Ran a prior-claims and records check on the claimant's vehicle. No earlier damage to the same areas is known, and nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the coverage start date on the policy.

Entry 7: Received the initial medical records. The treatment plan is a usual course for a soft-tissue neck injury of this kind, and the reported injury matches the type and force of the crash well. No earlier injury to the same body area is known from the records provided.

Entry 8: Requested an independent medical review of the records to check the treatment against the reported injury. The reviewer's preliminary comments indicate the care has been reasonable for the diagnosis.

Entry 9: Follow-up treatment notes show the claimant's physical therapy visits have been tapering off as symptoms improve. The provider's notes describe steady progress with fewer complaints at each visit.

Entry 10: Discussed the file status with the claims supervisor. Liability is clear on the insured's side, and the damage and injury picture is consistent with the reported facts, so the claim is moving toward a settlement evaluation.

Entry 11: Sent a status update to counsel requesting the final bills and the treatment summary. Settlement evaluation will be completed once those documents are received.
